learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge, understanding, and critical reasoning capabilities to evaluate the role played by digital media, social platforms, and AI in interpersonal and professional communication and relations, as well as some of their social, cultural and ethical implications in various settings.

Create, evaluate, and execute data-driven content strategies and specific assets tailor-made for clients' specific communication needs to connect with audiences and build and manage engagement, expertise and community.
Refine individual and group work ethics and skills to design and produce quality digital content strategies that consider cultural, ethical, sociopolitical and/or legal implications.

assessments.task_description:
There will be 5 in-class writing tasks held in the lecture beginning in week 6 (Tuesday 1/09/26) and concluding in week 10 (Tuesday 06/10/2026). This assignment will ask students to (a) critically reflect on some of the digital media theories, concepts, and topics discussed in the lectures in the previous weeks and briefly define the topic or concept in your own words; (b) apply the concept to a recent or historical real life case (from any type of organisation, public/government; commercial; NGOs, charities, and/or non-profits; brands or corporate). Students may use cases/examples mentioned in lectures, tutorials, recommended academic and/or professional readings, and/or from reliable media sites. The assignment may also ask students to (c) explain how the requested concept or topic can help make sense of existing and emerging technologies, and their role in our everyday life; and (d) and the way these may be used to address or resolve digital media issues. 

You will be given 20 minutes (5 minutes to prepare and 15 mins to write) to provide a handwritten answer of a maximum of 500 word that value 10 pts each. A glossary of key topics/concepts will be posted to Blackboard (Assessment and Learning Resources section) in week 3/4.  You are expected to identify, acknowledge and maybe informally reference some of the ideas, articles, or authors you studied for the task to demonstrate your engagement. Therefore, reading, understanding and applying weekly material and participating in discussions in lectures and tutorials will be crucial to obtain the maximum grade. This assessment evaluates students' own critical thinking and problem-solving capabilities, engagement with course topics, and academic knowledge. Writing Tasks will not be set on holidays, or in the case of unexpected events.

The Assignment Rubric will be posted to Blackboard in week 3/4. Also any additional or unanticipated changes will be posted to Bb and informed via email. Please check your university email regularly.

IMPORTANT NOTE 1: There will be 5 opportunities to take the In-Class Writing Task, but you only need to take 3 (valued at 10 pts each), which together may form a maximum of 1500 words to get a maximum of 30 pts. If you take more than 3 Tasks, we will select the best 3. This also means that you may miss up to 2 tasks without penalty. Paper deferrals or alternative assessment are not available except in very specific circumstances, such as a ‘Disability Action Plan’ in place, or other genuine (documented/supported) reasons (medical reasons, carer’s responsibilities, sudden accidents). So please, try to take as many as In-Class Writing Tasks as you can.

IMPORTANT NOTE 2: This assignment will be completed individually, in person, during lectures, and is handwritten. You must bring your own pen(s) to the lecture. We will provide a task-sheet (paper) where you will write your name, student number, tutorial group and/or tutor’s name, and your answer. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. So please engage with concepts and themes from the beginning. The use of electronics, generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) will not be permitted during the task. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Upon entering the theatre, you will be asked to place your bags, laptops, smart phones, tablets or other electronics below your seats, and place your student cards on your desk (visible position).

assessments.task_description:
The Digital Content Strategy consists of two parts:

  1. A 1400-word outline of your groups' strategic plan to create and produce digital content, stories, and assets for your selected client. This plan will inform your final portfolio.
  2. A 400-word Team AI Charter. The Team AI Charter is a written team agreement about how your group will and will not use AI tools to critically create, produce, and distribute content in the final portfolio. It should briefly address:
  • Authorship: Where does your creative contribution end and AI assistance begin? How will you endure authentic authorship of your work?
  • User Agreements: Which AI tools, if any, will you use, and for what specific tasks? What will you not use AI for? Support or justify.
  • Accountability: Explain how will your team ensure that all team members comply with the charter?

The content strategy will draw on the client brief, on your own research for the portfolios must, as digital plans must be data-driven, supported on evidence; and on some of the topics and practices discussed in lectures and workshops (e.g. strategic communication and content plan frameworks seen in classes). Your creativity and originality are crucial. 

You are asked to follow the content strategy template (that will be found on Blackboard, Assessment folder on week 4). The template will include a final section where you will briefly justify/support your choice of content and its potential effectiveness. Your digital content strategy must be concise and written and presented professionally and with clarity. 

The 'Digital Content Strategy' must be executed in groups consisting of 4/5 students max, with whom you will continue to work until the end of the semester when you will produce and execute the Portfolio (final assignment). Teammates must belong to the same workshop and have the same tutor. The groups will self-enrol to the Blackboard Groups section dedicated to this purpose (instructions on Bb in week 6). 

After the client briefing sessions, delivered in person and recorded in week 5 (during Lecture time), groups will be asked to choose one of the clients in weeks 6/7. Your group will work for that client for assignments 2 and 3.

Research work: To develop the plan (and the charter) you will research (a) the client organisation; (b) its digital content need or request; (c) its main audience(s) through 'social listening', building 'personas'; data, social media and/or sentiment analysis; metrics/analytics (if available); and desk research on relevant reports and other research tools and resources. The data you will collect will help you decide the best strategic content and digital tactics (text, visuals, graphs, other) that will boost engagement, impact, and ‘authority’ (expertise) for your client. Research will also be used to support and guide the Team AI Charter.

You will work collaboratively in your groups during workshops, following UQ group work recommendations (see Bb). In-class learning activities about creating content and using platform “Shorthand”, advantages and disadvantages of experimenting with AI, and collaborative learning will be applied. Through thinking and co-creating together, you will plan your projects to meet the client’s goal.

You are encouraged to use and reference recommended textbooks and relevant professional readings to support your content strategy plan (e.g., published reports on audience media habits, preferences and engagement in Australia and/or globally, some of which posted to Bb (see Learning Resources). 

Remember to cite all the material that is not originally yours (using APA 7th), and provide a reference list with the material cited at the end of your document (not included in the word count). Also include a cover page with the title of the assignment and your group's full names. Include a brief 'Introduction' section to your content strategy (with the aim of this paper). Written and visual presentation are key for digital communication must have professional and academic quality at the Master of Communication level. 

This assignment will be explained and practiced in lectures and workshops. 

This assessment task evaluates students' abilities, skills and knowledge. If you use AI or Machine Translation in any section of this strategy, even if just briefly, you will clearly acknowledge, justify and reference their use. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

assessments.task_description:
Portfolio - Group assignment

  • You will develop an integrated digital multimedia portfolio for your client. To complete this task you will bring together the capabilities in content planning and production that you have acquired throughout the semester. Your portfolio will critically consider contextual, cultural, ethical and /or legal factors that are relevant to your client's digital content needs. It will be informed by weekly activities (during lectures and workshops); the feedback you obtained from your tutors for assignment 2; and by the limits established by the team in their own Team AI Charter.
  • The pieces of content you will plan and produce for your portfolio strategically aim to build online engagement, impact, and 'expertise' for our client. The content should be data-driven, memorable, meaningful, and newsworthy. The task will be developed in groups (already self-enrolled on Bb for the Concept Plan) and will aim to respond to the client's brief (check client's brief and digital communication need or request). The portfolio should showcase a rich multimedia immersive, blog-type (or news style) story, copy, or text that will include a set of digital elements/assets (in writing, visual, and/or audio format) that must be well-articulated and coherent. The portfolio will be produced using Shorthand (training will be facilitated in classes and online). 
  • The story should have the potential to be deconstructed in various transmedia assets to be used via used in shared, earned, owned and paid media (e.g. posts, tiles, graphs, instastories). The Shorthand link (with password if any) must be copied to your report (and also to your Bb submission).

The portfolio submission will include:

a) Text in the form of a story in blog post style (800 words) written on the Shorthand platform. You will be telling a memorable, newsworthy, engaging story for your client. The story will strategically and effectively communicate/promote your client's message enhanced by digital tools to engage key audiences and build reputation/authority for your client. This story will include: Photo(s) - shot with your smartphone and/or professional equipment hired from MaPS; and/or taken from the client website, or free copyright websites;

b) A 90 seconds to 2 min-video (could be broken for example into two 1' videos) - shot and edited with your smartphone or professional equipment hired from MaPS; you may also use material from your client's website or free copyright sites (music, videos, animation);

c) An infographic or fact sheet with relevant information. Other type of graph(s) or statistics may be included.

d) All these items should be articulated in the Shorthand story’s layout; however, some assets may be submitted separately to Bb for better visualisation (if distorted on Shorthand). You will also suggest the use of the content you produce on other platforms (website, microsite, and/or social media platforms).

Separately, via Blackboard (which allows uploading multiple docs) you will also submit the following pieces: 

  1. Video script(s) - approx. 300 words (you may also include a podcast script if applicable; chat with the course coordinator);
  2. One-week media calendar (approx. 200 words). Calendar must be relevant to the project and consistent with dates provided by the client (if any).
  3. A 700-word Report that outlines and justifies the multimedia content strategy that you created to respond to the brief. This is an important part of the assignment. The Report will briefly describe the strategic process that led you to produce the multimedia content in the Portfolio and explain why this content is potentially effective to fulfil your client’s digital content needs. You will briefly discuss (just a few lines) any cultural, legal, or ethically relevant issues that may (or may not) be involved in the project. Important: you will briefly indicate how and why your group met or complied with the items included Team AI Charter.
  4. Cite any supporting material (use APA 7th). Include a cover page with the group names, title of the portfolio, make it visually appealing and consistent with the client’s look and feel, and a reference list at the end (these elements will not be included in the word count). Please note that the text in the report is different from the text in your Shorthand story (these are two different items).

SPECIAL NOTE 1: If you cannot, or do not want to produce a video, and upon consultation with the course coordinator, you may develop one or two mini 1-2-min informative (flash briefing) podcasts using your smartphone or MaPS' audio studio facilities. You will embed this podcast(s) in your Shorthand. You may also develop both, video and podcast if you are familiar with these techniques. Mixed media assets or texts are welcome.

SPECIAL NOTE 2: Class time will be spent on developing the skills required to create the portfolio. It is important that your take training or workshops provided by MaPS from week 2 onwards (e.g., Video production and editing; Photography, Audio Recording, etc. - see Blackboard for Calendar and registration). InDesign and WordPress may also help. MaPs offerings in semester 2 will be posted to Blackboard, Learning Resources in week 1. You can also use resources available via LinkedIn Learning Online Courses (UQ Library); Shorthand and Adobe Suite (both available to UQ students for free). The use of Canva is recommended for infographics, fact sheets, and calendars.

SPECIAL NOTE 3: Groups will informally Pitch their portfolio' digital strategy and main assets in workshops (5/6 mins per group + 4 min. for tutor feedback) in week 13 to receive feedback before final submission. Note that you will present just an overview of the strategy and main asset(s) (NOT the full portfolio). Presentations will be facilitated by your tutors and recorded for course admin purposes. More information relevant to this task will be posted to Bb. So, group pitches will be assessed by tutors (5 pts) during week 13 tutorials - More information on Blackboard.

SPECIAL NOTE 4: This assessment task evaluates students' human creativity, capabilities and knowledge preferably without the aid of Artificial Intelligence (AI). As some digital tools have embedded AI generated assets/material, you must acknowledge, justify and, if accepted, reference it in your work (via caption or footnote). If using AI, justify why its use is superior to original content created by you, or by the client. Also, reference, explain, support, and justify any AI use use in the Report section, and whteher it is consistent with the AI Team Charter. as otherwise student misconduct may apply. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Your human creativity, sensitivity, and critical thinking are central to this assignment.


Recording of Oral and Practical Assessment 

  • All presentations will be recorded for marking purposes via recording facilities available where the assessment takes place (eg. ECHO360, Zoom, camera device)  
  • Recordings will be retained by the School of Communication and Arts for at least 12 months from the release of the final grade for the course.  
  • Recordings will be stored in a secure manner and will only be accessed by authorised school staff for the purposes of: 
  • Moderation of marking;  
  • Provision of feedback to the student(s) recorded; and/or  
  • Re-marking following a successful re-mark application.

Week 13: Lecture (optional)

Optional: Room and time will be available for the delivery of some of the pitches (consult with tutors and course coordinator). Student pitches: 5/6 mins per group with 4 mins for feedback. Groups will present professionally and communicate clearly trying to connect with their audiences. 5 pts max. will be obtained.

Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
